label: Self-released
description: Chicago quartet's debut EP mixes big fuzzed-out guitar riffs with twangy pedal steel, mandolin, and bass harmonica. The four songs move from house-show stomp to honky-tonk shuffle, with abstract, personal lyrics giving the psychedelic country-rock an introspective edge. It plays like a scrappy, DIY-recorded take on '60s-'70s country-rock on a practice-space budget.
lineage: Self-described as a 'Country and Folk, Power Pop and Rock n' Roll' band drawing on 60s-70s country production, in line with the pedal-steel-and-fuzz indie-twang scene.

label: Ghost Ramp Records
description: GracieHorse's early full-length is billed on Bandcamp under alt-country and 'bummer jams' tags, a Los Angeles songwriter working a direct, unguarded confessional style over rock-leaning arrangements. Tracks like 'Youth is a Fire' and 'Tightrope' pair plainspoken, heartbreak-adjacent lyrics with a loose, road-worn band sound. It is the record that established the storytelling, no-frills approach she carried into her later work.
lineage: Sounds indebted to plainspoken alt-country and rock songwriting; early work from an LA singer-songwriter Bandcamp files under alt-country.

label: Self-released
description: Idle County bill themselves as 'WNC farm-rock' out of Asheville, and their debut LP is tagged country, alt-country, and rock n roll on Bandcamp. Song titles like 'Lebanon, TN' and 'Sin City' point to travelogue, small-town storytelling over a straightforward country-rock band sound. The plainspoken, guitar-forward feel recalls late-'90s alt-country.
lineage: Sounds indebted to '90s alt-country (Wilco/Uncle Tupelo-adjacent) as filtered through the 2020s Asheville scene.

label: Self-released
description: Jacob Tremont's ten-song junebug is tagged countrygaze alongside folk, acoustic pop, and lo-fi indie-folk on Bandcamp, a bedroom-recorded singer-songwriter set built around fingerpicked guitar and plainspoken lyrics. Song titles ('garden', 'diner', 'steamboat') suggest small, quiet vignettes rather than big statements. It's an intimate, home-recorded record from the hushed end of DIY singer-songwriter music.
lineage: Self-tagged 'countrygaze'; sounds akin to the hushed, DIY bedroom-folk wing of the current indie-twang scene.

label: Self-released
description: A six-song follow-up to junebug, carrying the same countrygaze/lo-fi indie-folk tags on Bandcamp. Tracks like 'no, i'm not afraid' and 'seven years of bad luck' continue the plainspoken, home-recorded singer-songwriter approach in shorter form. It reads as a between-albums EP rather than a full statement.
lineage: Sounds like a continuation of the countrygaze-tagged, DIY bedroom-folk sound of junebug.

label: Self-released
description: Billed a 'New York songman,' Josh Bolin's four-song debut EP is tagged cosmic americana alongside folk and indie rock on Bandcamp. The songs favor warm, unhurried arrangements over acoustic-and-electric guitar interplay, in keeping with the cosmic-country lineage of buttery lead guitar and easy tempos. It's a compact introduction rather than a full statement.
lineage: Tagged 'cosmic americana' by the artist; sounds indebted to the Gram Parsons/Laurel Canyon-descended cosmic country revival.

label: Self-released
description: This Canton, Ohio band's debut is tagged Americana, classic rock, and garage rock on Bandcamp, and its notes pitch a 'son-rock' aesthetic of heartland tunes and Rust Belt blues. 'On the Road Again, Again' sets a truck driver's meditations over a Willie Nelson-style loop. It's raspy, tape-hiss Midwestern rock about family friction and dead-end towns.
lineage: Self-described 'son-rock'; sounds indebted to heartland rock and Rust Belt Americana.

album: Blue heeler in ugly snowlight, grey on gray on gray on white.
label: Self-released
description: Kitchen, a solo bedroom-pop project from Rochester, New York, released this sprawling 20-track album, home-recorded and plainly designed. Songs like 'Real Estate Agent' pair conversational, self-lacerating lyrics with spare, lo-fi arrangements. It's DIY slacker songwriting rather than country per se, closer to the bedroom end of the Bandcamp indie-rock scene than to twang.
lineage: A solo lo-fi/DIY bedroom-indie project without an explicit country lineage; included here for its conversational, home-recorded slacker songwriting.
borderline_note: No overt twang/pedal-steel signifiers; included as DIY lo-fi/slacker (C7) rather than a stronger Core fit -- could arguably be Context instead.

label: Self-released
description: Local Superstar's self-titled album is tagged indie rock, alt-country, and folk rock on Bandcamp. Song titles like 'Passing By Waco', 'Dog Song', and 'Drinkin' to Write' point to loose, road- and drinking-song-flavored guitar rock. It's an eight-song set from a Savannah, Georgia project working the alt-country-leaning indie-rock lane.
lineage: Sounds akin to the current alt-country-leaning indie-rock scene of the Southeast.

label: Self-released
description: Lowell Thompson's ten-song Stranger's Advice is tagged rock, alt-country, and 'vermont' on Bandcamp. Songs like 'Bradley Street' and 'Meadow Lane' point toward plainspoken, place-named storytelling over straightforward alt-country arrangements. It's for listeners who like unfussy, band-backed songwriter records.
lineage: Sounds akin to the 2010s wave of indie-scene alt-country singer-songwriters.

label: Self-released
description: Wellington, New Zealand's Mudgoose tags this ten-song album lofi folk, outsider folk, loner folk, and experimental folk on Bandcamp. 'Mary's Lost' and the title track sit in hushed, homemade arrangements typical of the record. It's quiet, DIY loner-folk rather than country, closer to the lo-fi/outsider end of the current Bandcamp singer-songwriter underground.
lineage: Self-tagged loner/outsider lo-fi folk, part of the DIY Bandcamp network rather than a country lineage.
borderline_note: No explicit twang; included via the DIY/lo-fi trunk (hushed loner folk) rather than a country signifier.

label: New Rose
description: Los Angeles band New Rose's eleven-song Morning Haze is tagged 'country' on Bandcamp, with a tracklist ('Country Noise', 'Should've Been A Wedding', 'Pearl Buttons') that reads as a set of plainspoken country-rock songs about heartbreak and small betrayals. It's a straightforward, guitar-and-twang alt-country record from an LA band.
lineage: Self-tagged 'country,' part of the current alt-country-leaning West Coast indie scene.

label: Self-released
description: Washington, DC's Heaven Forbid bill themselves 'High Faultin' Rootin' Tootin' Sons of Guns', and their eight-song debut album is a straightforward honky-tonk record mixing originals with country classics such as 'Make The World Go Away'. The band's own copy promises '8 new favorites and country classics in high fidelity'. It's for listeners who want classic honky-tonk played straight by a young band.
lineage: Sounds indebted to classic honky-tonk and '60s country standards.

label: Self-released
description: Alabama songwriter Jameson Hubbard's debut album under the name Haysop is billed in its notes as a rock 'n' roll album through and through. It pairs Muscle Shoals-flavored guitar and Wurlitzer with Hubbard's deadpan-tinged, Kurt Vile-esque songwriting about a budding relationship. It's a 13-song set that swings from full-throttle rockers to loose front-porch picking.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Muscle Shoals-style Southern soul-rock and Kurt Vile's drawled songwriting.

album: American Ecology / April 26, 2024 / Should I Have Another Beer
note: Strong Core fit (Oakland alt-country/countrygaze band with Appalachian roots) but every release found on Bandcamp is a 3-track EP or single (below the 4-song threshold); no qualifying LP/EP found within budget.
